Subject: Kickoff: dedicated capacity for Fathom.ai (early numbers)

Hi Lauren / Marissa,

Thanks for taking time earlier. We want to move from trial to a Dedicated reservation for our summarization+search product. High-level ask: predictable latency under p99 800ms, and predictable monthly cost with reserved capacity.

Quick context:
- Customer: Fathom.ai (NLP SaaS)
- Current hosted usage: ~180 reqs/min average, big spikes during US business hours
- Typical prompt tokens (user query + system): ~80 tokens
- Typical response tokens (summaries): 600–800 tokens; occasional long-run jobs (~2k tokens) for nightly batch summarization
- Auth/session model: short-lived sessions (stateless API per request); no sustained KV across many requests today

Can you send your dedicated-sizing worksheet so we can fill and attach a traffic sample? Also critical: we operate in us-west and need to understand multi-region failover options.

Thanks — Alex

Hi Alex — great to hear. I attached our dedicated_sizing_template.xlsx to this thread; it walks through the fields we use to model GPU footprint. Below is a condensed questionnaire to accelerate the sizing model — if you can paste answers inline we can run an initial estimate today.

1) Peak sustained QPS (per AZ) during business hours (15–60 minute windows):
2) Burst multiplier (how many x above peak for 1–15 minute spikes):
3) Fraction of requests that are short chat-like (<=200 response tokens) vs long summarization jobs (>1k tokens):
4) Average prompt tokens and average response tokens (separately for short/long):
5) Percent of requests requiring context lookups (database/embeddings) pre-inference:
6) Acceptable p99 latency (ms) and target p50 for interactive flows:
7) Peak concurrent sessions (if stateful) or concurrency expectation for stateless API:
8) Nightly batch jobs per hour (count and typical token counts):
9) Preferred region(s) and any compliance constraints (e.g., data residency):
10) Any existing SLAs or outage windows we should model for DR/failover

Notes on modeling: we typically estimate token processing throughput using sample traces (thanks for offering traffic_samples.csv). For long-tail responses (2k+ tokens) we often recommend a separate batch profile or larger instance class to avoid impacting interactive p99s. We also give a 'burst pool' recommendation (small autoscale cushion) to handle 2–5x short spikes.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-min sizing call today at 11:30 PT to walk through values.

Lauren — thanks, attaching traffic_samples.csv with an hour of weekday peak traffic (UTC timestamps). Answers inline below:

1) Peak sustained QPS per AZ: 3.2 reqs/sec (~192 reqs/min) during main business hour in us-west
2) Burst multiplier: we see up to 4x for short windows (~5–10 minutes) during marketing pushes
3) Request mix: ~82% short (<=200 tokens responses) and ~18% long (>1k tokens)
4) Average tokens:
   - Short: prompt 70 tokens, response 320 tokens
   - Long: prompt 120 tokens, response 1,850 tokens
5) Context lookups: ~30% of requests call our embeddings search prior to generation
6) Latency goals: p99 <= 800ms for short flows; p99 <= 4s acceptable for long summarization (we can batch overnight for biggest runs)
7) Concurrency expectation (stateless): avg concurrency during peak AZ ~55 concurrent inflight requests; bursts push to ~210 concurrent inflight
8) Nightly batch: 3 jobs, each processes ~10k documents (avg 1.2k tokens per doc) — jobs run in a 2–3 hour window overnight
9) Region: us-west primary; also want warm-failover to us-east (no strict residency)
10) SLAs: we need 99.9% monthly uptime for production.

A few extra notes: we plan to use quantized Llama-2-70B variant for long summarization and a 13B optimized generator variant for interactive. We'd like Redwood to recommend instance SKUs and a committed capacity figure we can propose to finance.

— Alex
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Grant <alex@fathomai.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Kickoff: dedicated capacity for Fathom.ai (initial sizing and next steps)

Alex — thanks for the sample and the clear answers. Quick summary of our initial thinking and next steps.

Summary (initial, conservative):
- Workload profile: ~192 reqs/min sustained per AZ (~3.2 rps), average tokens weighted mostly toward short flows but with a non-trivial long tail (18%). Burst tolerance needed up to ~4x for ~10 mins.
- Recommended baseline fleet (reserved): 4 x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs (reserved capacity) configured as a mixed pool: 2 GPUs hosting the 13B interactive model (low latency priority, aggressive KV caching) and 2 GPUs optimized/quantized for the 70B summarizer (higher mem, throughput-oriented).
- Autoscale/ burst pool: allow autoscale to 6 GPUs with a warm standby for 15-min bursts to keep p99 for interactive under 800ms.
- Batch plan: run the nightly 3 jobs on the summarizer pool with scheduling windows and preemptible burst capacity if needed; we estimate batch throughput will use ~30–40% of summarizer capacity overnight.
- Networking/DR: we recommend active-primary in us-west with a passive warm-failover in us-east (cross-region caches disabled by default; we can replicate model artifacts to both regions).
- Cost note: the above maps to a committed monthly baseline with an expected uplift for burst hours; we'll provide a cost run and a few alternative configs (smaller instance mix, higher oversub) in the formal proposal.

Next steps:
1) Lauren will turn these inputs into a quantitative sizing sheet and estimated GPU-hours / month (I already queued the template).
2) We'll run an internal micro-benchmark using the traffic_samples.csv to validate p99 assumptions (esp. mixed short+long token mix).
3) Proposal delivery: draft by Tue, Feb 16; include SKU breakdown, pricing, and recommended SLA options.

Action: Alex — can you confirm whether you want encryption-at-rest with customer KMS (this affects Private deployment pricing) and whether nightly batch docs can be processed in a different project/namespace?
